skills.name: storytelling-truth-and-vividness
skills.description: Provides an ethical framework for nonfiction storytelling (the Five Permissible Lies) and techniques for creating vivid mental imagery (Cinema of the Mind). Applies when a founder is crafting a company origin story, preparing a keynote, refining a customer case study, or deciding how much to compress or omit from a real narrative. Use when the question is not what to say but how truthfully and vividly to say it.

skills.name: what-is-a-story
skills.description: Defines what qualifies as a genuine story versus an anecdote, romp, or report. Teaches the transformation requirement, the Dinner Test, and the personal-narrative principle. Use when a founder's pitch feels flat despite good content, when team presentations list facts without landing emotionally, when someone confuses a sequence of events with a compelling narrative, or when preparing any communication that must move people rather than merely inform them.

skills.name: building-thinking-strength
skills.description: Develops the four internal muscles required for clear thinking -- self-accountability, self-knowledge, self-control, and self-confidence -- using the Clear Thinking strength-building system. Covers setting personal standards above external requirements, choosing exemplars, building a personal board of directors, and practising in sandboxes. Use when blaming external factors for poor outcomes, struggling to say no under social pressure, lacking the confidence to execute a difficult decision, noticing that team standards have drifted toward mediocrity, or seeking a structured approach to personal operating system design.

skills.name: defining-and-exploring-problems
skills.description: Teaches the discipline of correct problem definition and structured solution exploration before any evaluation begins. Covers the problem-solution firewall, root cause identification, the premortem, second-order thinking ('and then what?'), binary thinking traps, integrative Both-And options, and opportunity cost analysis through the 3-Lens Principle. Use when a team is jumping to solutions before understanding the problem, when a founder suspects they are treating symptoms rather than causes, when only two options seem to exist, when opportunity costs are unclear, or when first-conclusion bias is narrowing the solution space.

skills.name: enemies-of-clear-thinking
skills.description: Diagnoses the four biological defaults that hijack entrepreneurial judgment -- emotion, ego, social conformity, and inertia -- using the Clear Thinking framework. Maps how each default manifests in startup contexts and provides recognition patterns for identifying when autopilot has seized control. Use when reacting impulsively to bad news, defending a position for ego rather than merit, conforming to industry consensus without independent analysis, or resisting a necessary pivot despite mounting evidence.

skills.name: evaluating-and-deciding
skills.description: Covers the full arc from option evaluation through execution and post-decision learning: criteria weighting and the 'most important thing' discipline, high-fidelity and high-expertise information gathering, margin of safety as a buffer against being wrong, the irreversibility test for calibrating decision speed, bullets-before-cannonballs experimentation, execution fail-safes (trip wires, commander's intent, Ulysses pacts), and the process-over-outcome principle for decision journals. Use when evaluating multiple options against competing criteria, when the cost of being wrong is high and margin of safety is needed, when deciding how fast to move, when building execution safeguards, or when conducting post-mortems that separate luck from skill.

skills.name: managing-weakness-and-mistakes
skills.description: Provides a systematic approach to protecting against predictable decision failures and extracting maximum learning from errors, using the Clear Thinking safeguard architecture and mistake-handling protocol. Covers knowing your weaknesses (biological and acquired), building safeguards (prevention, automatic rules, friction, guardrails, perspective shifts), and the four-step process for handling mistakes without ego contamination. Use when repeating the same errors across decisions, needing to design pre-commitment rules for high-pressure situations, building organisational error-recovery processes, or recognising that a cover-up is compounding an initial mistake.

skills.name: wanting-what-matters
skills.description: Addresses the meta-question behind all decision-making: whether the entrepreneur is optimising for the right things. Covers the hedonic treadmill and 'happy-when' trap, Dickens's A Christmas Carol as a decision-making parable, what happiness research from the elderly consistently reveals, memento mori as a practical decision filter (the deathbed test), the regret-minimisation framework, and the distinction between ordinary moments and defining moments. Use when a founder suspects they are chasing metrics that do not produce satisfaction, when strategic priorities feel misaligned with personal values, when mortality awareness could sharpen decision-making, or when the question shifts from 'how do I get what I want?' to 'is what I want worth wanting?'

skills.name: clarity-and-concision
skills.description: Teaches techniques for achieving relentless clarity and ruthless concision in business writing, including the 20-word sentence rule, concrete detail over abstraction, word economy tactics, and the reader's perspective test. Features extensive before/after examples demonstrating how bloated corporate prose can be cut by 50-70% without losing meaning. Use when tightening any business document, eliminating wordiness, improving readability scores, preparing executive summaries, or when writing feels vague or overlong.

skills.name: grammar-and-mechanics
skills.description: Provides a structured reference for the grammar and punctuation rules that most frequently undermine credibility in business writing. Covers subject-verb agreement, pronoun case, dangling modifiers, parallel construction, comma splices, and the most common usage confusions (affect/effect, that/which, who/whom). Use when proofreading pitch decks, investor updates, client proposals, or any external-facing document where a single error can erode perceived competence.

skills.name: plain-language-and-flow
skills.description: Teaches how to eliminate corporate jargon (bizspeak), use chronological ordering for factual accounts, and create smooth document flow through transitional words, signposting, and paragraph continuity. Features a bizspeak blacklist, before/after translations of corporate prose, and a taxonomy of transitional phrases. Use when writing sounds too corporate, when documents lack narrative flow, when readers report confusion about the sequence of events, or when establishing plain-language standards for an organisation.

skills.name: reader-psychology
skills.description: Teaches the cognitive science behind how busy readers actually process written communications. Covers working memory limits, the F-pattern scanning behaviour, selective attention, and the four-stage triage process readers apply to every message. Use when diagnosing why communications fail to land, designing high-stakes messages for distracted audiences, auditing existing copy for cognitive overload, or training a team to write with the reader's brain in mind.

skills.name: revising-and-editing
skills.description: Teaches the distinct disciplines of revising (rethinking content and structure) and editing (refining sentences and word choices), with a concrete three-draft evolution showing how a mediocre memo transforms into an excellent one. Covers revision checklists, editing checklists, and the peer feedback process. Use when polishing any business document, preparing final drafts for stakeholders, training teams on writing quality, or establishing editorial review processes.

skills.name: tone-and-engagement
skills.description: Diagnoses and corrects the tonal failures that cause business writing to anaesthetise readers rather than persuade them. Addresses passive voice, nominalizations, hyperformality, sarcasm, and the specific calibration of tone to audience and relationship. Use when drafting client communications, revising documents that feel lifeless or overly formal, preparing sensitive messages that require tonal precision, or building writing standards for a team.

skills.name: writing-effective-emails
skills.description: Provides a practical system for writing emails that get read, answered, and acted upon. Covers subject line craft, optimal length, formatting for scanning, tone calibration, CC/BCC etiquette, and when to choose a different medium entirely. Use when composing high-stakes emails to investors or clients, establishing email standards for a team, preparing sensitive written communications, or diagnosing why outreach emails receive poor response rates.

skills.name: writing-for-navigation
skills.description: Provides a structural system for arranging written content so busy readers can find what matters within seconds. Covers BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front), visual hierarchy, headings as signposts, bullet point strategy, formatting discipline, and the map metaphor for document design. Use when structuring investor updates, redesigning internal communications, formatting product announcements, or diagnosing why well-written messages still fail to land.

skills.name: writing-for-response
skills.description: Teaches how to write messages that convert reader understanding into reader action. Covers friction reduction, default design, the power of constrained choices, response-oriented formatting, and the 30-second response test. Use when crafting calls to action in emails or product copy, designing opt-in or enrolment flows, diagnosing low response rates on surveys or meeting requests, or building templates for action-oriented team communications.

skills.name: writing-memos-and-reports
skills.description: Provides a systematic approach to structuring memos, reports, and business letters that inform decisions and drive action. Covers the Issue-Solution-Reason summary framework, the Who-Why-What-When-How planning chart, visual aids, three-audience writing, and business letter conventions. Use when drafting board memos, internal recommendations, market analysis reports, strategic proposals, client-facing letters, or any document longer than an email that must survive scrutiny from multiple readers.

skills.name: writing-performance-reviews
skills.description: Guides the high-stakes process of writing performance appraisals that are specific, fair, legally defensible, and genuinely useful for employee development. Covers the seven evaluation dimensions (attitude, efficiency, human relations, judgment, knowledge, reliability, communication), the spectrum from superb to poor, the discipline of pairing evaluative language with concrete evidence, and the legal implications of imprecise writing. Use when preparing annual or quarterly reviews, designing performance evaluation templates, training first-time managers on review writing, or auditing existing review practices for fairness and consistency.

skills.name: writing-process
skills.description: Teaches the MACJ writing process -- Madman, Architect, Carpenter, Judge -- a four-phase method for producing effective business documents by separating idea generation, organisation, drafting, and editing into distinct sequential tasks. Covers brainstorming, outlining in sets of three, speed writing, and disciplined revision. Use when facing writer's block, struggling to organise complex material, drafting reports or proposals, or when any business document feels overwhelming to start.

skills.name: writing-with-purpose
skills.description: Teaches how purpose and audience analysis determine the form, tone, and content of every business communication. Applies the principle that the same facts, addressed to the same reader, produce radically different letters depending on the writer's objective. Use when drafting any business document, preparing investor updates, writing customer communications, crafting fundraising emails, or any situation where the writer is unsure what tone to strike or how to frame a message.
